design.oneComposer: Every customer-readable address line in hauska-map now goes through composeSitusLine, and the MCP's label through appendMissingSitusComponents. The reason is the defect's own shape: three sites composed the same line three ways and each dropped a different component. A second copy of the rule could drift the same way, so the rule lives once per repo and the test file is named for the clause (situs-address.p270.test.ts, situsCompose.test.ts).
design.inferredCityLabelling: situsCityBasis carries 'cad-roll' or 'city-limits'. Where it is 'city-limits' the display provenance gains the note 'city whose limits contain this parcel (the county roll states no situs city)', so the card says WHAT the city is rather than presenting a jurisdiction city as the roll's mailing city. An unincorporated parcel with no roll city and no cityLimits value names no city at all.
design.noInventionRule: A city is inferred ONLY when the roll's own situsCity rail is present, served, and reads a DECLARED absent-verified absence. Unslated, refused, legacy-transitional and malformed all yield no city, and a test enumerates all four. A ZIP is carried only from a served string cell; absent/refused/malformed cells are not turned into a ZIP.

adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.attack_composerCorruptsGoodLines: ATTEMPTED REFUTE: appending could duplicate components, or mangle a line that already reads in full — MITIGATED, and the mitigation is measured not asserted: hasCity/hasState/hasZip are segment- and substring-aware (state is matched only as a whole comma segment so a street named 'TX AVE' is not read as a state), the byte-identical cases are pinned by test, and the pre-existing share-header case still passes unchanged.
adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.attack_stateZipOrder: ATTEMPTED REFUTE: appending 'TX 78660' to a line that already ends in ', TX' would produce '..., TX, TX 78660' — CAUGHT during the build by this lane's own test (expected '..., TX 78660', got '..., TX'): the ZIP now rides with its state as a suffix when the state is already present. This is the one defect the pre-registration did not anticipate and the tests found.
adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.attack_inventedCity: ATTEMPTED REFUTE: the cityLimits fallback could name a jurisdiction city on parcels whose ledger row never asked for a city — MITIGATED by conditioning the fallback on the roll's OWN declared absent-verified verdict, and by a test that an unincorporated parcel names no city.
adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.attack_envelopeAddressDrift: ATTEMPTED REFUTE: composedSitusAddress feeds the live-derive POST, so a changed line could change what the derive answers for a parcel and move the envelope — ACCEPTED AS A REAL COUPLING. The exposure is bounded to lines that were dropping components: those parcels previously POSTed a bare street and now POST a street with its city and ZIP. Every already-complete line is unchanged. This is also the intended direction (a bare street is the weaker key). Named so the integration seat reads the post-deploy env-* envelopes for the subjects it grades.
adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.attack_shareViewBypass: ATTEMPTED REFUTE: the dispatch's three-question gate asks what BYPASSES the composition. The sweep found one: sharePropertyHeader served the raw street to the anonymous share view. NOT a false alarm — it was the same defect on a customer surface — and it is fixed in this lane's second commit rather than left as a note.
adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.attack_silentInertZip: ATTEMPTED REFUTE: if the live /record does not serve a situsZip rail for 48453, this lane's ZIP carriage is inert while the probe still PASSes on the city — a green that hides a dropped component, which is the program's named defect class. RESIDUAL, declared rather than argued away: the probe cannot grade a ZIP the payload does not carry (the dispatch defines the predicate that way), so the gap is closed by MEASUREMENT instead — the three situs rails are named in COMPOSED_RECORD_RAIL_KEYS, which makes the payload's own recordRailStates report what the reader served for each, and the probe already records that map into the artifact. The post-deploy artifact therefore carries railStates.situsZip.serve as a fact, not a claim. See openThreads.
adversarialReviewCheckpoint1.verdict: ACCEPTED with one declared residual (the live situsZip rail serve state) and one coupling named for the integration seat (the live-derive address key).
